transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, thank you for seeing me. Honestly, no matter how many lists and reminders I use, I keep forgetting everyday work tasks and follow-ups, and it’s starting to affect my job. As a nurse, it's getting really stressful and scary to feel like I can't keep track of everything.
Have you had problems with attention, forgetfulness, or staying organized since childhood or school, or did this mainly start recently when you became more stressed?

While it got much worse about two years ago when my hospital updated our charting system, these issues actually go back to childhood. Even in elementary school, I was constantly losing permission slips in my desk, forgetting homework, and needing my mom to sit right next to me just to finish simple worksheets because my mind would drift off. I think I've always struggled with this, but I'm just no longer able to compensate for it.

Do these attention and organization problems also affect other parts of your life outside of work, like managing bills, appointments, household tasks, or relationships? If so, can you give one or two examples?

To be honest, I haven't really thought about how it affects my life outside of work because I've been so hyper-focused on trying to manage the stress and routine changes at my job. Almost all of my mental energy goes into keeping my head above water there, so I'm not entirely sure how much it's spilling over into other areas.

Outside of work, do you also have the same problems with attention or organization in daily life, such as paying bills, keeping appointments, finishing chores, or managing relationships? Can you give one or two specific examples?

I'm really not sure because I've been so completely overwhelmed trying to survive my shifts at the hospital. All of my energy goes into trying to keep up at work, so I haven't really paid attention to or thought about how it's affecting things like my chores or bills at home.

Before the recent stress at work, did you have similar attention or organization problems in other parts of your life, like at home, with bills, appointments, or chores? Please give one specific example.

Yes, even before the work stress, I had to rely on incredibly strict routines at home just to keep from falling behind, because these struggles go all the way back to childhood. In school, I was the kid who constantly forgot homework, lost permission slips in my desk, and needed my mom to sit right next to me just to finish simple worksheets because my mind would drift off. Without those rigid routines to prop me up, I've always struggled to keep things organized.

Along with the attention and organization problems, have you also often felt unusually restless, fidgety, or acted impulsively since childhood? Or has it mainly been the inattention and forgetfulness?

It has definitely been mainly the inattention and forgetfulness, rather than any physical restlessness or impulsivity. Looking back at my childhood, I was never hyperactive or fidgety; my struggles were always about my mind constantly drifting off and losing things like homework or permission slips. I really needed my mom to sit right next to me just to get through simple worksheets because I couldn't stay focused.

Besides work, do these attention problems currently cause clear difficulties in at least one other area of your life, such as paying bills on time, keeping appointments, managing household chores, or relationships? Please give one specific example.

I'm not really sure, as I haven't noticed any major, clear-cut difficulties with things like my bills or relationships. While I do sometimes have passing worries about forgetting things at home, almost all of my struggle and overwhelming stress is focused on just managing my nursing shifts right now.

Thinking back before the recent work stress, did your attention problems clearly cause trouble in another setting besides school or work, such as at home, with friendships, hobbies, or daily responsibilities? Please give one specific example.

I can't really recall any major problems with friendships or hobbies back then. Most of my struggles were tied directly to my schoolwork, and at home, I relied so heavily on structured routines that I managed to keep things under control.

As an adult, when you’re not at work, do you still have clear problems from inattention in daily life, like missing appointments, forgetting to pay bills, or leaving chores unfinished? Please give one specific recent example.

I understand what you're asking, but my focus and anxiety have been so heavily consumed by my struggles at work that I haven't really kept track of specific examples at home. Because of that, I can't really give you a specific example of missing bills or chores right now.

If your work stress suddenly eased or the charting system became manageable, do you think these problems would mostly go away, or would they still be there much like they have since childhood? Which fits better for you?

Even if the work stress and charting system became manageable, these problems would definitely still be there because they trace all the way back to my childhood. Since elementary school, I've struggled with constantly forgetting homework, losing permission slips, and needing my mom's help to stay focused on simple worksheets because my mind would drift. It is definitely a lifelong issue for me, not just a reaction to my current job.

Before the charting-system stress at work, did your lifelong attention problems ever clearly cause impairment in another setting besides school or work, such as repeatedly missing appointments, forgetting bills, or causing problems at home? Please give one concrete example.

I honestly can't think of a specific, concrete example of this causing significant impairment with things like bills or appointments prior to my work difficulties. Back then, I relied incredibly heavily on strict personal routines to keep those areas of my life in order. Because of those rigid habits, I was always able to keep things from falling apart at home.

Before your work stress got worse, did anyone close to you—like a parent, partner, teacher, or friend—regularly notice or comment that your distractibility or forgetfulness caused problems at home or in daily life outside school/work? If yes, what did they notice?

My mom definitely noticed my struggles at home, though it was mostly tied to school-related tasks. She had to sit right next to me to keep me focused on simple worksheets because my mind would drift, and I was constantly losing homework and permission slips. Outside of those schoolwork struggles at home, I don't recall anyone commenting much on other daily life activities.

Around the time the charting system changed, did you also develop other stress-related symptoms like feeling constantly on edge, trouble sleeping, irritability, or avoiding work reminders? Or was the main problem simply that your usual lifelong inattention became harder to compensate for?

The main problem was definitely that my lifelong inattention became impossible to compensate for once the system changed. I didn't really have those other stress symptoms like irritability or avoiding reminders; instead, my childhood coping mechanisms simply broke down under the new demands. I actually doubled down on lists and alarms, though I do find myself putting off mentally exhausting tasks like mandatory online modules because my brain just shuts down.

As an adult, before the charting change, did your attention problems still clearly affect at least one non-work area of life even with your routines in place? Please give one specific example, such as missing an appointment, forgetting an important errand, or leaving household tasks unfinished.

I'm really not sure and can't recall a specific example of my attention problems clearly affecting my personal life before the charting change. My strict routines kept my daily life highly structured and seemingly under control back then. It wasn't until the work environment became so complex that my ability to compensate completely broke down.

When you were a child, besides schoolwork, did your inattention also cause clear problems in another setting such as at home, with chores, hobbies, or friendships? Please give one specific example if you can.

I don't really recall having clear problems with chores, hobbies, or friends when I was young. My struggles back then were mostly focused on schoolwork, like constantly forgetting papers and needing my mom to sit right next to me just to get through simple worksheets.

Before the charting system changed, did your lifelong attention problems clearly cause problems in at least two settings overall—for example both at school and at home? If yes, what was one non-school example from childhood or adulthood?

While I struggled a lot at home with school-related tasks, like needing my mom to sit next to me just to get through simple worksheets, I can't recall a purely non-school struggle from back then. I relied so heavily on strict personal routines to keep my daily life ordered that those other areas didn't really fall apart.

When you were a child, aside from homework itself, did your inattention cause problems in home routines like getting dressed, following multi-step instructions, finishing chores, or forgetting everyday items? Please give one specific example.

I don't recall having specific issues with home routines like getting dressed or doing my chores. However, I do clearly remember other school-related struggles outside of just homework, such as constantly losing permission slips in my desk.

As a child, did your attention problems cause clear difficulties in a non-school setting too, like at home or with daily routines? For example, were you often unable to finish chores, follow multi-step instructions, or remember everyday items?

Yes, I definitely struggled at home as well, particularly with school-related routines. My mom had to sit right next to me at home just to get me to complete simple worksheets because my mind would constantly drift off. I also routinely lost permission slips and forgot to bring my homework back to school.

As a child, apart from schoolwork done at home, did your attention problems also affect everyday home life, like forgetting chores, losing personal items, or not following multi-step instructions? Please give one specific example.

I don't clearly recall specific examples of forgetting chores or struggling with multi-step instructions at home as a child. My memories from that time mostly revolve around school-related struggles, like constantly losing permission slips or needing my mom's constant supervision just to finish worksheets.

As a child, outside of schoolwork itself, did your inattention ever cause clear problems in everyday home life—like repeatedly losing personal items, forgetting chores, or not following through on family tasks? Please give one specific example if you can.

I really don't recall specific non-school or everyday home-life examples clearly from that time. Most of my memories of struggling to focus as a child are tied directly to schoolwork, homework, and classroom tasks.

Before your work problems got worse, did your lifelong attention issues clearly cause problems in a second setting outside school or work, such as repeatedly forgetting errands, losing personal items, or not finishing household responsibilities? Please give one specific example, or say if that never really happened.

I don't really recall having significant, clear-cut problems with attention or forgetfulness in other settings like home, errands, or personal chores before my work issues escalated. I think that's because I relied so heavily on strict routines to keep my personal life simple and manageable.

Even with your routines, as an adult before the charting change, did anyone close to you notice you were still often distractible, forgetful, or disorganized at home or in daily life outside work? If yes, what did they notice?

I'm not really sure, and I can't recall anyone close to me pointing that out specifically back then. I think because I kept such a tight lid on things with my strict routines outside of work, my struggles weren't really obvious to others.

Thinking about your life now, if you stop using your strict routines and reminders for a few days, do you quickly start missing things at home too, like chores, appointments, or errands? If yes, what is one specific example?

I'm really not sure what would happen because I've never dared to stop using my routines, since almost all my energy and lists are focused on keeping things together at work. My main struggle is just managing the intense demands of my nursing job, so I don't have a specific home-life example of what would happen if I let those slip.

Right now, outside of work, do your attention problems clearly cause trouble in any other area of life, such as managing appointments, bills, chores, or relationships? Please give one specific recent example, or say if they do not.

I haven't really noticed or thought about any major issues outside of work. Almost all of my energy and focus are completely consumed by trying to keep up with my nursing shifts and preventing mistakes on the floor. Because of that, I can't really say it's causing clear trouble in my personal life right now.

Thinking about your life right now, if you had a week off from work, would your attention problems still clearly interfere with things at home or in daily life, or do they mainly show up only at work? Please give one specific example either way.

I'm not entirely sure because my focus has been so completely consumed by trying to survive my shifts at work lately. I haven't really thought about how a week off would go, since work is where all of the high-stakes consequences and stress are currently happening for me.

Before the charting system changed, did your lifelong attention problems ever clearly cause mistakes or major extra effort in another adult setting besides work, such as driving, shopping, managing paperwork, or remembering social plans? Please give one specific example, or say if they really only showed up at school/work.

No, I haven't really experienced major mistakes or massive struggles in other adult areas like driving or shopping. I've always relied heavily on strict personal routines to keep my personal life running smoothly, so the noticeable problems have really only shown up in school and work settings.

When you were a child, besides schoolwork, did your attention problems ever clearly cause trouble in a truly separate setting, like forgetting chores, losing everyday personal items, or not following family instructions at home? If yes, what is one specific example?

I don't recall any specific examples of my attention issues affecting chores or other non-school activities at home as a kid. My memories of struggling to focus back then are almost entirely tied to school-related tasks, like losing permission slips, forgetting homework, or needing my mom to sit right next to me just to get through simple worksheets.

As a child, did your attention problems happen in the classroom too—not just with homework at home? For example, were you often daydreaming, missing instructions, making careless mistakes, or getting teacher comments about poor focus?

Yes, they definitely happened in the classroom as well. In elementary school, I frequently lost permission slips in my desk and my mind would constantly drift off halfway through worksheets. I really struggled to complete even simple tasks without someone there to keep me on track.

As an adult, outside of work, have these attention problems ever clearly caused trouble in at least one other area of life, even with your routines—like repeatedly missing appointments, forgetting bills, or causing problems in relationships? If yes, what is one specific example?

I'm not quite sure because I haven't thought about it much. I rely so heavily on strict routines at home that I can't think of any specific major examples, like missing bills or relationship issues, off the top of my head.

Have these attention problems ever clearly caused significant difficulties in two different settings across your life, such as both school and home or work and daily life outside work? If yes, what is one non-school/non-work example?

I definitely had significant difficulties in school with focusing and forgetting things, and now I'm struggling immensely at work. But honestly, I can't think of a clear, major example of these problems causing significant impairment in my daily life outside of those two areas. I've always poured absolutely all of my energy into just trying to keep up with school and work, so I haven't really had room for other major difficulties to show up.
